note: M3b requires every reachable portable branch in the named semantic classes to carry a reviewed disposition. This file IS that review. A branch with no entry fails tools/coverage/check.mjs; an entry for a branch that has since become covered is STALE and also fails, so the table cannot rot into a list of excuses.

dispositionMeanings.required: A portable behavior the corpus should discriminate and does not. This is an owed case, not an accepted gap.
dispositionMeanings.excluded: Not reachable through any behavior the JS port implements, or not a behavior at all (defensive branches, unreachable defaults).
dispositionMeanings.nonportable: Reachable in Java but with no JS counterpart by design — JVM-only APIs, Java type-system artifacts, display tooling the plan defers.

excludedClasses.why: A vendored JSON parser. The JS port does not reproduce it — M5a wrote a bounded parser with different structure, whose own behavior is gated by tools/parse-diff against LocalizedStringLoader.parse rather than against MinimalJson's internals. Its branches are implementation of a dependency, not portable semantics. 127 branch points across 15 classes.

classDispositions.why: A class-level disposition, used here because all 62 branches across all seven methods implement ONE thing: LocalizedString.toString(). Verified rather than assumed. (1) The class is private and its single instantiation is LocalizedString.toString() at LocalizedString.java:125. (2) Its output is not a diagnostic message — no format() call anywhere in com.lokalized interpolates a LocalizedString, a PlaceholderDefinition, a LanguageFormTranslation or an ExpressionTranslation, so none of 'LocalizedString{key=', '<cycle#', '<ref#', '<unknown-placeholder-definition>' or '<unsupported-language-form>' can ever reach a caller through an exception or a warning. (3) The JS port emits none of those strings (grepped src/ for each). (4) JAVA-SURFACE-AUDIT.md and plan v7 line 3155 disposition LocalizedString as 'Validated LocalizedStringInput/defined frozen model, not a runtime class' — a frozen plain object with no toString override. I did NOT lean on plan 3.7's deferred-tooling sentence, which is about Cardinality/Ordinality display-example inspection and does not cover this class.

The 4096-character bounded StringBuilder that DiagnosticRenderer writes into, including its surrogate-pair-safe truncation marker placement. THE DAG MEMOIZATION RULE, and only one of its four branches is covered. Plan v7 section 3.6 specifies it in full: validation 'may skip a reused subtree only when the cached depth is greater than or equal to its current entry depth; a subtree first seen shallower is revalidated when reused deeper'. The throw arm is arithmetically unreachable. `materializedPrecision` is `precision + max(0, effectiveScale - scale) + max(0, compactExponent - effectiveScale)` (PluralOperands.java:415-427). TranslationRuntimeLimits caps precision at MAXIMUM_NUMBER_PRECISION 4096, |scale| at MAXIMUM_ABSOLUTE_NUMBER_SCALE 4096, visible decimal places at 4096 and compact exponent at 4096, and the Builder validates each against the ACTIVE limits before this point. Maximizing over effectiveScale: if effectiveScale >= compactExponent the last two terms sum to effectiveScale - scale <= 4096 - (-4096) = 8192; otherwise they sum to compactExponent - scale <= 4096 + 4096 = 8192. So the total is bounded by 4096 + 8192 = 12288 — exactly MAXIMUM_MATERIALIZED_PRECISION — and the guard tests `>`. The supremum is attained (e.g. a 4096-digit unscaled value written as `<4096 digits>E+4096`, scale -4096, with compactExponent 4096), so the constant is a backstop that sits precisely one unit above anything the other limits admit. Worth a human's eye: if the intent was 'reject at the ceiling' the comparison should be `>=`; as written the check can never fire.

AUDIT: reclassified from required. `member.weight <= 0` at the head of the survivor-serving loop cannot be true for a member that HAS survivors. Members are sorted by descending weight (DefaultStrings:1561), so a group's representative holds the group maximum, and `activeMembers[i]` is set only when `Double.compare(members[i].weight, members[representative].weight) == 0` — every active member therefore carries exactly the representative's weight. A survivor exists only where the governor sweep found `effectiveWeight > 0`, and its selection index is either the governor itself or that governor's representative, both of which carry that same positive weight. The original disposition's premise — 'the governing member and the selection-position member differ across an alias group' — is right about the divergence but the two members still share a weight, so the guard is defensive.

AUDIT REVERSAL (was 'required'). A wildcard member's survivors and its structural filter are computed by the SAME predicate: cells come from structurallyMatches(member.rangeSubtags, localeStatics.tagSubtags) at languageRangeSpecificityFor:2041, and structurallyFilteredLocales re-runs structurallyMatches(range, locale.toLanguageTag()) over those same locales. A wildcard member therefore cannot own a survivor that its own filter rejects, and the empty-filter arm has no input. What the entry wanted to protect -- that a wildcard range is never broadened into semantic matching -- is instead pinned by m3b-negotiation.extension-singleton-stops-structural-walk, where `de-*-phonebk` structurally fails against a loaded de-u-co-phonebk and the answer is NONE rather than a CLDR-inferred locale. The entry previously also cited .structural-filter-rejects-nonmatching as covering structurallyFilteredLocales' rejecting arm directly. That was FALSE and is removed: the coverage data reports :2343 at 1 of 2 branches with that case in the corpus, and this table's own :2343 entry concludes the rejecting arm has no reachable call site. The case is still valuable -- it discriminates a port that skips structural filtering -- but it does not close that branch, and its own note has been corrected too.

AUDIT REVERSAL (was 'required'). A private-use member without a wildcard is given a cell by languageRangeSpecificityFor ONLY through the EXACT test at 2038 (`localeStatics.languageTag.equalsIgnoreCase(member.structuralRange)`); every later rung is cut off by the private-use return at 2035. So any survivor of such a member has a tag equal to the range, and line 1823's exact-source loop returns it before line 1855 is reached. The behaviour the entry wanted -- that `x-foo` never broadens into an ordinary primary language `x` -- is pinned instead by m3b-canonicalization.private-use-not-maximized (x-private selects only its own catalog) and m3b-negotiation.private-use-wildcard-matches-structurally (a wildcard is what re-admits a private-use range to extended filtering).

AUDIT REVERSAL (was 'required'). The primary-language tail of matchFor (lines 1886-1925) is UNREACHABLE, so no case can be owed for it. Proof, and it contradicts the original entry's suggested case: (1) control reaches line 1882 only for a member that is not a bare wildcard (1826), not undetermined-without-private-use (1819), not wildcard-bearing (1841) and not private-use (1855); (2) for such a member `CldrLocaleData.languageScriptForLikelySubtag(semanticRange)` is ALWAYS present -- likelySubtagCandidateTags always ends with `und`, `und` is in the pinned likely-subtags table, and all 7,788 entries in that table carry a script (verified against vendor/lokalized-java/src/build/resources/cldr/cldr-locale-data.json), so the only way lookupMatchByLikelySubtag returns empty is an empty matchingLocales; (3) getting past 1893 with a non-empty `candidates` then requires some survivor with normalizedLanguage == primary AND hasCompatibleLikelyScript, and compatibleLikelyScripts is equality-or-null while neither side can be null for a locale with a non-empty language -- so compatible implies equal, and that survivor would already have been in matchingLocales, contradicting (2). The coverage data agrees: line 1882 is 1/2 and every line below it is 0/2, i.e. the tail is not merely unsatisfied but never entered. Empirically I drove the review's own suggested input, `pt-AO`/`pt-MZ` against loaded pt-BR/pt-PT, plus zxx (a language absent from the likely-subtags table) with three regional catalogs, plus sr-Latn against a Cyrillic-only sr catalog: every one resolves through CLDR parent fallback or likely-subtag matching, or returns NONE at 1896's precondition, and none reaches the tail. What the tail's tiebreaker walk was owed to protect IS covered elsewhere -- lookupMatchByLikelySubtag and preferredLocaleForRange both consult the same tiebreaker list, and construction guarantees a list for every loaded language.

RE-CLASSIFIED required -> nonportable (M3b owed-case authoring pass). Two independent reasons, either sufficient. (1) NO JS COUNTERPART BY DESIGN. Plan v7 fixes the runtime limits at Java's documented defaults and ports TranslationRuntimeLimits as 'Fixed v1 values; customization rejected and no public mutable builder' (plan surface table); CreateStringsBehaviorOptions declares `runtimeLimits?: undefined` and plan 4.6 makes a non-undefined value a construction-time ConfigurationError. The port therefore never constructs limits: there is no builder, no nullable setter, and no per-limit validation to perform. lokalized-js tools/conformance.mjs encodes the same contract, attributing every diverging runtime-limit fixture to 'runtime-limit overrides are not implemented' as a standing v1 deferral rather than as owed work, and the plan names custom runtime-limit builders as an explicit v1 deferral -- which is exactly what `nonportable` covers. (2) NOT DISCRIMINABLE THROUGH THE ORACLE even if it were portable; see below. If a later version exposes limit customization, these entries return to `required`. This arm is `builder.maximumNumberPrecision(null)`, the boxed-Integer 'null restores the documented default' shape -- a Java type-system artifact of a mutable builder with @Nullable Integer setters. VectorOracle.runtimeLimitsFrom reads every member with JsonValue.asInt(), which throws on a JSON null, so no fixture can call the setter with null; and a fixture that OMITS a limit never calls the setter at all, so the arm is unreachable from the corpus in both directions. The behaviour the arm produces -- the documented default -- is already pinned many times over: 24 of the 25 runtime-limit fixtures set one or two limits and leave the other eight or nine absent (only runtime-limits-ceilings sets all ten), and their cases assert default behaviour on the rest. What remains unpinned is only the Java-only distinction between an explicit null and an absent value. || ORIGINAL ENTRY: 'null RESTORES THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT' for maximumNumberPrecision. The oracle harness only calls a setter when the fixture names that limit (VectorOracle.java:194-195 plus runtimeLimitsFrom), so the null arm is never taken: every one of the 22 runtime-limit fixtures sets its limits explicitly. This arm requires a cause if and only if the failure reason is RESOLUTION_FAILURE.
